programme.title: Volcom Presents: Escramble
programme.desc: In a time beyond and close to now... a vision was revealed. A vision of the very first dream of life. The dream of life before there was life. The dream that vapor dreams of becoming solid and falling to meet whatever will catch and hold it. Thus begins "ESCRAMBLE". Featuring Bjorn Leines, Terje Haakonsen, Mark Landvik, Wille Yli-Louma, Shaun White, Seth Huot, Gigi Rüf, Erik Leines, Bryan Iguchi, Chris Demolski and Jamie Lynn.

programme.title: Volcom Presents: 9191
programme.desc: 9191 is a sideways introspective into the bewildering snow-covered dreamscape of international time traveler and mystic of the shred - Gigi Rüf.

programme.title: Absinthe Films Presents: Isle Of Snow
programme.desc: Join us as we explore the snowboard world through the perspectives of the people who live it and have made it their lives follow their passions.

programme.title: The Manboys Movie
programme.desc: The boys are back with new friends and a brand new snowboard film. The Manboys Movie will definitely top your expectations. Featuring bangers from Chris Rasman, Rusty Ockenden, Craig McMorris, Jody Wachniak, Matt Belzile, Anto Chamberland, and Mark Sollors.

programme.title: The ManBoys Presents: Snowdance
programme.desc: Snowdance is a backcountry snowboarding film. Because even if you’ve never set foot in the backcountry, you can still be grateful that it’s there. Seven years and one pandemic since their fruition, The ManBoys roster still remains largely intact with Chris Rasman, Rusty Ockenden, Matt Belzile, Jody Wachniak, Beau Bishop & Eric Jackson. Snowdance was filmed by Ben Webb, Connor Winton, Dave Craig, and Ryan Kenny.

programme.title: Air Time Podcast - Shin Campos
programme.desc: Shin, the timeless powder hound, has been an iconic presence since the late '80s. With a career spanning decades, he's not only witnessed, but lived through it all. From a gritty renegade in Whistler, crafting local videos with his homies, to scaling the peaks of snowboarding stardom with Tree Top, Absinthe, Standard, White Out, and more. He briefly ventured into mountain guiding but a tragic incident led him to a new path. Today, Shin orchestrates cinematic magic behind the lens, skillfully managing and producing awe-inspiring commercial shoots that dominate the sea-to-sky landscapes. Although he's moved on from professional snowboarding, his passion remains unwavering. Shin's story epitomizes passion, resilience, and evolution. Enjoy the show!

programme.title: Absinthe Films Presents: Dopamine
programme.desc: Dopamine is a naturally occurring chemical produced by the human brain, which controls movement and reward. In the world of progressive snowboarding, the joy of physical movement and the reward of being outside are the two greatest factors motivating riders to evolve and innovate. The Absinthe Films documentary Dopamine captures professional snowboarders pushing boundaries and chasing storms across the Chilkats, Valhallas, Monashees, Dolomites, and Pyrenees mountains.

programme.title: La Zone
programme.desc: In the early 2000's, snowboard filmer David 'Vlad' Vladyka and a handful of riders discovered an off-the-radar area on the French-Swiss border that held massive potential for shooting freestyle snowboarding. The mountain pass featured rolling terrain punctuated by steep roll overs that are perfect for building jumps. The area was Le Col de Cou, and though it had a name, the riders called it 'La Zone', a purposefully vague nickname that would help them keep the area a secret. Over the next decade, La Zone would become one of the most productive and standard setting locations for filming freestyle snowboarding in all of Europe. Shots from La Zone were featured in several Absinthe films, and many others. Now 20 years later, Jones team rider Mat Schaer and Vlad still return to La Zone to film from time to time, but the pristine slopes they enjoyed in the past are much harder to find as Le Col de Cou has become a popular ski touring destination. Featuring new and historic footage from La Zone, this new short film directed by Julien Rosens, and produced by Absinthe Films, highlights the history, beauty and inevitable evolution of this legendary shred spot. Credits LA ZONE, a movie directed by Julien Roserens Produced by Absinthe Films Supported by Jonessnowboards, Region Dents du Midi, Doodah store Edited by Jules Guarneri Soundmix by Stephane Chapelle Graphics by René Zumstein Photo by Michael Cordey Music : Tugrul by Ochre, Rhea by Yehezkel Raz, Where It Beginns It Ends by Be Still The Earth, Strange Life de YGGL, Let Us Get Out by Redder

programme.title: Hook Down, Wheels Down
programme.desc: Produced in the early 1970s, "Hook Down, Wheels Down" was one of the most comprehensive (and expensive) films made by the U.S. Navy. It covers the history and development of the U.S. aircraft carrier, and does so through interviews with many of the men who made it happen. While dozens of aircraft carriers are featured, it is the USS John F. Kennedy (CV-67) that takes center stage -- and the material shot on her deck looks like it is right out of "Top Gun". There is wonderful flight op footage, great aerial flight footage, incredible WWII dog fightand bombing footage as well as endless aircraft carrier operational footage. Also shown in this film are very rare images of the first aircraft carrier USS Langley (CV-1) (formerly collier USS Jupiter AC-3). The follow on vessels are widely featured including USS Lexington (CV-3) and the USS Yorktown (CV-5) in the Battle of Coral Sea. Also featured: USS Saratoga (CV-2), USS Enterprise (CV-6), USS Hornet (CV-8), USS Wasp (CV-7), USS Ranger (CV-4), USS Yorktown (CV-5), USS Essex (CV-9), USS Guadalcanal (CVE-60), the British carrier HMS Furious, the destroyer USS Zeilin (DD-313), and many other warships. Various incidents are shown from Pearl Harbor, Midway, Coral Sea, the capture of the submarine U-505, the Marianas Turkey Shoot, the Doolittle Raid on Japan, and more. Includes interviews or appearances by many WWII naval aviators and aces including Wade McClusky, John Jay Courtney, Billy Mitchell, Gerald Bogen, Leslie Generes, John S. Thatch (of "Thatch Weave" fame), Ensign George Gay, David Campbell (whose Minsi III appears in the film), Edward "Butch" O'Hare, Charles Lindbergh, Glenn Curtiss, Clark Gable and Wallace Beery. Planes seen in the film include the Wright Brothers flier, biplanes, Lindbergh's Spirit of St. Louis, the NC-4 Flying Boat, Hellcat, Avenger, Corsair, Vindicator, Devastator, Wildcat, and Japanese Zero. Also seen in the film: dogfights, combat flying, the Washington Conference on battleships, the Panama Canal exercise of 1929, air mail service.

programme.title: US Carrier Fights for Life - USS Yorktown Battle of the Coral Sea World War II

programme.desc: The “new navy” is the focus of this 1969 educational documentary presented by the United States Navy — “The Attack Carrier: From USS Langley CV1 to USS Enterprise CVAN65.” The color film traces the development and history of aircraft carriers used by the United States Navy. Aircraft that have been used by the Navy, such as the Grumman A-6 Intruder and McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II, also are featured.

programme.title: USS New Jersey (BB-62)
programme.desc: Written by historian Richard Hough and presented by the U.S. Navy, the late-1960s film The American Dreadnought gives viewers a brief history of the American battleship USS New Jersey and a solid background of this class of ship. The film opens by taking viewers to the spring of 1921 where planes sink battleships as part of the agreement to cease battleship production following World War I. The film then cuts to 1966 and shows viewers retired battleships sitting idle at a remote pier in the Philadelphia Navy yard. The three ships are the Iowa, Wisconsin, and New Jersey.

programme.title: World War II Victory Ship Film

This first part of the narrative focuses on its initial mission to transport a large shipment of U.S. Army cargo, including railroad car wheels, underframes, and eight locomotives, from San Francisco to a destination somewhere across the Pacific.

programme.title: WWII US Coast Guard film- Task Force

programme.title: America's Cup Race- Sailing Ships
programme.desc: This late 1930s or early 1940s film AWAY WITH THE WIND features various ships and water activities. It includes rare footage of clipper ships at the 10 second mark, and square riggers. Fishing on the Grand Banks is seen at the 1:00 mark. The Gertrude L. Thebaud is seen at the 1:08 mark. This is an American fishing and racing schooner built and launched in Essex, Massachusetts in 1930. A celebrated racing competitor of the Bluenose, it was designed by Frank Paine and built by Arthur D. Story for Louis A. Thebaud, and named for his wife, Gertrude Thebaud. programme.desc: Casper emerges from a subway station, following a crowd of scared strangers. They capture Casper, like Lilliputians did to Gulliver, then place him in a cage on wheels, in which they tow him to the Ruler of the Moon, King Luna. Then animated trees attack the city of the moon men. The moon men defend their fortified city with flaming missiles. The tree monsters fight back with water, then break through the town walls. When the fight seems lost to the tree monsters, Casper escapes his cage, and helps the moon men. Casper goes underground. The friendly ghost then pulls trees' parts through the moon surface and ties them together, immobilizing the trees. The frustrated trees writhe and strain against the knots Casper has tied. Casper and the moon men have won. Then, and only then, does King Luna embrace Casper as a friend. King Luna knights Casper for the valiant defense of his people. Then all the moon men join in singing the Casper theme song.

A sucker is hauled off the street and sat down at a card game; he dashes off as soon as someone shouts "they found gold in the hills" but others stake claims before he can. He ends up chopping off a cliff, falling down, and landing in the hospital. The doctor gives him news of another gold strike and he rushes out to begin panning. After some more mining gags and a song, we see a montage of more failed gold strikes. Back to the present day, where the storyteller claims to have sworn off gold, until a rider passes through with news of another strike, when he trades the station for the car and sets out after the gold.

programme.title: A Haul in One 1956
programme.desc: Popeye and Bluto are, believe it or not, pals and partners in a moving company. (Maybe it's because Popeye isn't squinting here.) Anyhow, Olive has made the mistake of hiring them. She hasn't finished packing yet, so the boys, smitten as soon as she answers the door, compete to help her. Once packed, they compete to move more impressive piles of her belongings. Popeye easily wins these contests, even though Bluto locks him in the van at one point. At the end, Bluto socks Popeye into the piano, then into a table; though he hardly seems to need it, Popeye still eats his spinach, then thrashes Bluto.

programme.title: Auto China: Driving future of mobility
programme.desc: Auto China 2026 opens on April 24, showcasing nearly 1,500 vehicles over 10 days – at a pivotal turning point for China's automotive industry. Amid commodity volatility and fractured supply chains, electrification is no longer a question of “if” but “how fast.” As the world’s largest electric vehicle (EV) market and a major force of global EV sales, how is China shaping the pace and direction of this charge towards greener, smarter vehicles? Join us on BizTalk this week as we explore how China and Germany are moving in step toward the next phase of the future of mobility.

programme.title: From Island Farms to Cloud Power, From Mountain Hubs to Urban Beats
programme.desc: From tropical coffee aromas to high-tech computing hubs, how is China defining "high-quality development"? In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the fields of Wanning, Hainan, where a small coffee bean becomes a symbol of the Free Trade Port’s opening-up, to the mountains of Guizhou, where a 14-millisecond data latency is powering the rendering of global blockbusters like Ne Zha 2. Finally, we dive into the vibrant Livehouse scene of China’s megacities, exploring a $1.2 billion "emotional economy" that is reshaping urban nightlife. From solid digital infrastructure to the rhythmic energy of the music scene, this episode captures the heartbeat of China’s evolving economic future.

programme.title: PRISMA
programme.desc: Prisma es un programa cultural producido por CGTN en español en colaboración con el multimedio de comunicación latinoamericano teleSUR. Su objetivo es mostrar a los televidentes la riqueza cultural de China y el mundo hispanohablante, elevar el conocimiento de la cultura china en los países de habla hispana y establecer una plataforma de diálogo entre ambas partes. Se trata de un programa mensual de 30 minutos de duración que comenzó a emitirse en agosto de 2016. Está compuesto de tres segmentos que destacan por su diversidad temática. Primero, un espacio de noticias culturales; después, una semblanza de alguna personalidad del ámbito cultural latinoamericano; y finalmente un documental sobre aspectos de la cultura china.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of milu deer
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River
programme.desc: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River is a documentary focusing on the World Heritage sites and cultural–ecological conservation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Through the lens of Ningxia’s heritage stories, the film highlights China’s commitment to World Heritage preservation, ecological restoration, and cultural continuity — presenting to global audiences a land where history and modernity intertwine, and where desert and oasis coexist. By following the guardians of the Western Xia Imperial Tombs, desert restorers in the Tengger Desert, Great Wall rangers at Sanguankou, traditional sheepskin raft craftsmen, and managers of the Yellow River irrigation system in Qingtongxia, the program reveals Ningxia’s distinctive contributions to cultural heritage, natural ecology, and intangible traditions — and the enduring human spirit behind them.

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: Awakening Lion
programme.desc: Xingshi, or literally “awakened lion,” is a name for the southern style of the lion dance. Historically, it evolved from a court dance in the Tang Dynasty almost 1,200 years ago. With the southward migration of the population from the central plains, lion dance culture was introduced to the south. In the Ming Dynasty around 400 years ago, xingshi appeared in Guangdong and was then widely spread throughout southern China and even overseas. Lion dance has become a very important part of Chinese culture.

programme.title: CULTURAL INHERITORS Inheritance matters more than fame
programme.desc: The Vibe production team's meticulously crafted documentary series "Cultural Inheritors". The eight episodes span across various regions of China, focusing on the inheritors and artists of intangible cultural heritage. They explore and innovate with artisanal dedication, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship of fields such as the Ru Kiln porcelain, colored stone inlay, Pu'er tea, and Lingnan woodwork. Let’s embark on a cultural journey together, savoring the beauty of tradition and embracing the spirit of intangible cultural heritage!

programme.title: Miao Embroidery: History in Stitches
programme.desc: According to legend, during a migration by the Miao ethnic group, a female chieftain wanted to keep a record of all the mountains and lakes she passed along the way. The means she chose of doing so was by stitching the images on her dress. By the time they reached a suitable place to settle, her clothing was covered with embroidered designs. This, it’s said, was the origin of Miao embroidery. As the story tells us, the designs in Miao embroidery are closely related to the natural world and daily life. The Miao people have a special fondness for nature. So, as well as depicting their daily farming and work activities, they copy birds, flowers, mountains, and grass onto their clothing. Over the years, the embroidery of the Miao people has become a written record of their life. The stitches are like characters which, when many of them are combined, become a record of their history, their collected wisdom, and the knowledge passed down from their ancestors.

programme.title: Quyang Stone Carving
programme.desc: Quyang is known as a hometown of Chinese carving. Quyang's stone carving works are popular around different parts of China, thus also exported to over 100 countries and regions worldwide. The style of Quyang stone carving both carries the mysterious and rough spirit of the Wei Dynasty and the natural and graceful forms of the Tang and Song dynasties. It reflects the life experiences and live philosophies of local artisans. Each statue's showcases unique oriental aesthetics.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of milu deer
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River
programme.desc: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River is a documentary focusing on the World Heritage sites and cultural–ecological conservation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Through the lens of Ningxia’s heritage stories, the film highlights China’s commitment to World Heritage preservation, ecological restoration, and cultural continuity — presenting to global audiences a land where history and modernity intertwine, and where desert and oasis coexist. By following the guardians of the Western Xia Imperial Tombs, desert restorers in the Tengger Desert, Great Wall rangers at Sanguankou, traditional sheepskin raft craftsmen, and managers of the Yellow River irrigation system in Qingtongxia, the program reveals Ningxia’s distinctive contributions to cultural heritage, natural ecology, and intangible traditions — and the enduring human spirit behind them.

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: Awakening Lion
programme.desc: Xingshi, or literally “awakened lion,” is a name for the southern style of the lion dance. Historically, it evolved from a court dance in the Tang Dynasty almost 1,200 years ago. With the southward migration of the population from the central plains, lion dance culture was introduced to the south. In the Ming Dynasty around 400 years ago, xingshi appeared in Guangdong and was then widely spread throughout southern China and even overseas. Lion dance has become a very important part of Chinese culture.

programme.title: CULTURAL INHERITORS Inheritance matters more than fame
programme.desc: The Vibe production team's meticulously crafted documentary series "Cultural Inheritors". The eight episodes span across various regions of China, focusing on the inheritors and artists of intangible cultural heritage. They explore and innovate with artisanal dedication, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship of fields such as the Ru Kiln porcelain, colored stone inlay, Pu'er tea, and Lingnan woodwork. Let’s embark on a cultural journey together, savoring the beauty of tradition and embracing the spirit of intangible cultural heritage!

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive in Changsha — the economic and cultural hub of Hunan Province, and a core city in the Yangtze River Middle Reaches Economic Zone. Our lens turns to the "Xiangjiang Ladies" who work in Changsha’s high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors. Their daily lives and professional endeavors reflect the city’s innovative vitality, while their after-work gatherings also showcase the dazzling night views along both banks of the Xiangjiang River, highlighting Changsha’s distinct charm as a vibrant capital of leisure and entertainment.

programme.title: The Art of Harmony: Human Becoming
programme.desc: “The Art of Harmony” is a documentary about Confucianism, produced by CGTN and Discovery Channel. It highlights the timeless nature of the sage’s philosophy and its global relevance today. Join us in exploring how the world might benefit from the pursuit of “The Art of Harmony”.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the " Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programme.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programme.title: Young star on green field
programme.desc: Meet Sun Chenxi, a 12-year-old soccer "star" from Ningbo who first picked up the game at the age of four and is already playing with the confidence of a veteran. Sun says he dreams of turning pro one day and leading China's men's team to the World Cup. Dribbling and passing with skills far more advanced than his age, he has won over audiences far and wide after his father posted clips of Sun flashing his fancy footwork on social media. The soon-to-be-teenager now has millions of followers online. Already recognized as a rising young talent, high hopes are pinned on Sun as he is cheered on by his parents, friends, and throngs of fans online.

programme.title: Celadon Ou Music
programme.desc: Celadon ou music is also called "bowl music.” The reason is that the ancient Chinese word for bowl sounds like ou. The music originated simply as improvised rhythms tapped out on bowls. It was this spontaneity that made celadon ou so popular. Celadon ou music was at the height of its popularity over 1,100 years ago. But with time, it faded from history. At one point, it was even on the verge of being lost forever. After hundreds of years of obscurity, it re-emerged at the end of last century.

programme.title: Kesi
programme.desc: Silk is a classic symbol of Chinese culture. It helped opened up economic and cultural exchanges between East and West and witnessed the spread of Eastern civilization to the world. As a representative of traditional Chinese silk art, kesi is renowned for its highly ornamental weaving techniques of highlighting warps and breaking wefts, and has been deeply loved by people for thousands of years. In folk culture, it enjoys the reputation of “an inch of kesi is worth an inch of gold.”

programme.title: Miao Silverware: A Shining Epic
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the fascinating world of the silver-working art of the Miao ethnic group. Join us, and hear the stories and see the works of four remarkable individuals. From a national-level inheritor who is preserving the traditional craft, to an artist infusing personal flair into his designs; from a female silversmith imbuing her work with feminine warmth, to a young artisan inspiring a new generation, we investigate the rich heritage, cultural significance, and evolving potential of Miao silverware.

programme.title: A Toda Luz
programme.desc: ¿Te hace falta ánimo o quieres crecer en tu fe junto a otros? A Toda Luz es un programa lleno de vida, con conversaciones reales, risas, y verdades que inspiran. Con voces dinámicas y temas relevantes, te anima, te conecta y te acerca más a Dios.

programme.title: Afroman | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Afroman lit up the Bitcoin Conference stage in Las Vegas with a performance unlike anything else this year. After his house was raided and his money seized, he discovered that freedom of speech and Bitcoin were the tools he needed to fight back. In this set, he announces his 2028 presidential campaign, calls for jury trials in family court, and performs live renditions of "Because I Got High" and "Lemon Pound Cake." Don't miss this raw, hilarious, and unexpectedly powerful moment from Vegas.

programme.title: Tim Draper's Bitcoin Warning: A Run on the Banks Is Coming | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The dollar is changing faster than most people realize. In this powerful keynote from The Bitcoin Conference in Las Vegas, legendary venture capitalist Tim Draper of Draper Associates explains why holding Bitcoin has shifted from opportunity to necessity. Drawing from his Mount Gox losses, his record-setting U.S. Marshal's Office auction bid, and decades of experience in Silicon Valley, Draper lays out the case for a dollar-to-stablecoin-to-Bitcoin transition.

programme.title: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins Bitcoin 2026 Fireside Chat
programme.desc: For the first time in history, a sitting SEC Chairman took the stage at the Bitcoin Conference. Paul Atkins joins Perianne Boring of The Digital Chamber on the Nakamoto stage in Las Vegas to detail a complete 180 in how the agency views digital assets. He breaks down the new joint token taxonomy with the CFTC, the SEC's reinterpretation of the Howey Test, and the upcoming innovation exemption that will let firms experiment with on-chain securities and token fundraising in the United States. If you want to understand where U.S. digital asset regulation is actually heading, this is the conversation.

programme.title: Fireside: CFTC Chairman Mike Selig | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For more than a decade, Bitcoiners and developers have lived under regulatory uncertainty and sometimes outright hostility from Washington. In this fireside conversation, CFTC Chairman Mike Selig joins Gregory Xethalis to explain how the agency has used its first 100+ days to end regulation by enforcement, launch Project Crypto with the SEC, and protect software developers building on Bitcoin. Selig breaks down the new joint taxonomy guidance, the no-action letter for self-custodial wallets, and why pending market structure legislation is essential to future-proof the asset class.

programme.title: Code is Free Speech: Ending the War on Bitcoin | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For years, Bitcoin developers wrote code with one eye over their shoulder. That era is officially over. At Bitcoin 2026, Coinbase Chief Legal Officer Paul Grewal sits down with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel to break down the April 7, 2025 DOJ memo that ended regulation by prosecution and what it means for builders, platforms, and the future of digital asset policy in the United States. They get into Tornado Cash, Samourai Wallet, the FBI's offshore scam compound takedowns, and why both DOJ leaders are personally Bitcoin holders.

programme.title: Arthur Hayes Bitcoin 2026 Keynote: 21 Weeks Later
programme.desc: The Iran war, AI replacing knowledge workers, and a new Fed Chair pick have markets confused. Arthur Hayes thinks most macro analysts are reading the tea leaves wrong. In this presentation, the BitMEX co-founder walks through why he's turned bullish on Bitcoin, why Kevin Warsh isn't the hawk people fear, and how a quiet April 1st banking regulation could unleash trillions in fresh credit. Hayes lays out a year-end Bitcoin target of $125,000 and explains the wartime money-printing thesis driving him there

programme.title: From American Hashrate to Wall Street: How Bitcoin Benefits The U.S. | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Bitcoin just crossed the bridge into Wall Street and the boomer money is finally moving. In this Bitcoin Conference panel, Bloomberg's Eric Balchunas sits down with Eric Trump of American Bitcoin and John Koudounis of Calamos Investments to unpack the $60B Bitcoin ETF wave, the $146 trillion in advised assets still sidelined, and the $124 trillion generational wealth transfer about to reshape every portfolio. Eric Trump tells his debanking story and explains why the Trump Organization went all-in on Bitcoin. John Koudounis breaks down Calamos' 100%, 90%, and 80% protected Bitcoin ETFs.

programme.title: Mark Moss: Building a Personal Treasury with a Perpetual Bitcoin Machine | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: You bought the right asset, but are you playing the wrong game? At Bitcoin Vegas 2026, Mark Moss of Market Disruptors argues that most Bitcoiners are still operating with a fiat mindset and will quietly lose the wealth game even with Bitcoin in cold storage. He unpacks the Cantillon effect, the macro debt loop, and a five-step "Perpetual Bitcoin Machine" designed to build a personal treasury that compounds for generations. If you've ever wondered how much Bitcoin you need to retire, this talk reframes the entire question.

programme.title: How Will Bitcoin Behave with Global Uncertainty? | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The Fed is changing hands, the Middle East is on fire, and private credit is starting to crack. Natalie Brunell sits down with Danielle DiMartino Booth (QI Research), Joseph Wang (Fedguy.com), and Matt Hougan (Bitwise) for a no-holds-barred debate on how Bitcoin behaves when the global order gets shaky. They cover Kevin Warsh's incoming Fed chairmanship, stagflation risk, and why Wall Street might be far more complacent than it should be. If you care about where macro and Bitcoin intersect, this is essential viewing.

programme.title: What's the Price of Freedom? Ask "The Six Billion Dollar Man" | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: What happens when an award-winning documentary about Julian Assange wins Cannes and a Golden Globe and still no streamer or network will touch it? Filmmaker Eugene Jarecki joins Jack Dorsey at Bitcoin 2026 to reveal how the Bitcoin community is stepping in where legacy media refuses to. They trace the line from Wikileaks' 2011 banking blockade, through Edward Snowden, to a Global Watch Party designed to bypass media censorship entirely.

programme.title: The Wives & Mothers Carrying The Fight Against Injustice | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The state came for the men they loved and these three women stepped onto the battlefield. Lauren Rodriguez (wife of jailed Samourai Wallet co-founder Keonne Rodriguez), Janice McAfee (widow of John McAfee), and Lyn Ulbricht (mother of pardoned Silk Road founder Ross Ulbricht) sit down with Efrat Fenigson to talk pardons, privacy, and what it really takes to fight the U.S. government from the outside. This is one of the most powerful conversations on Bitcoin, civil liberties, and the war on privacy you'll hear all year. Watch, share, and don't forget the prisoners.

programme.title: Multiple Paths, One Asset: Spend, Borrow, or Hodl? | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Jack Mallers and Miles Suter rarely share a stage and when they do, the gloves come off. Danny Knowles moderates this panel on whether Bitcoin should be spent, borrowed against, or held forever, with Strike pushing dollar-denominated Lightning payments and Block rolling out Tap to Pay across every Square merchant in America. The conversation gets into Saylor's borrowing strategy, the chicken-and-egg problem of Bitcoin merchant adoption, and why card network rewards are the real obstacle. If you care about Bitcoin payments, lending, or the future of peer-to-peer cash, this one is essential.

programme.title: Paolo Ardoino Keynote: Tether - A Psychohistory Implementation | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: What if a stablecoin company was actually building the foundation for civilization? In this Bitcoin Conference talk, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino borrows from Isaac Asimov's Foundation to explain why Tether is investing in Bitcoin, peer-to-peer protocols, self-custodial wallets, and decentralized AI. He breaks down the open-source Resilience Stack: Hole Punch, Keet, WDK, and QVAC SDK and why 4 billion unbanked people are at the heart of the mission.

programme.title: Are We Getting More Clarity? | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The CLARITY Act could be the most consequential piece of Bitcoin and digital asset legislation in U.S. history, and it's hanging in the balance right now. In this panel from the Bitcoin Conference, Senators Cynthia Lummis and Bernie Moreno join Patrick Witt of the White House, Sam Kazemian of Frax, and Miles Jennings of A16z crypto to break down why market structure matters, what's at stake for Bitcoin, and how the Genius Act paved the way. They also discuss the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, the CFTC's role, and the geopolitical stakes of ceding crypto leadership to China.

programme.title: Senator Cynthia Lummis on the Clarity Act and America's Bitcoin Future | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Senator Cynthia Lummis takes the Bitcoin 2026 stage to deliver a clear message: the Clarity Act is heading to markup in May, and the United States is positioning itself as the global capital for Bitcoin. She walks through the early Senate battles including the absurd IRS attempt to classify software developers and miners as brokers and explains how the Bitcoin industry's response shaped policy. With her time in office winding down, this keynote is both a victory lap and a roadmap.

programme.title: Keynote: Michael Saylor | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The credit market just got a new heavyweight. In this keynote, Michael Saylor reveals how Strategy engineered STRC, a Bitcoin-backed preferred stock that grew into the largest and most liquid preferred in the world in under eight months. Saylor breaks down the math behind 11.5% tax-deferred yields, why private credit is melting down, and how digital credit is set to cannibalize trillions in legacy capital markets.

programme.title: Keynote: Jack Mallers - The Bitcoin Company | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: What does the ideal Bitcoin company actually look like? In this Bitcoin 2026 keynote, Jack Mallers CEO of Strike and Twenty One wears both hats to unveil a strategic merger with Tether's mining arm Electron and a slate of new Strike products including Volatility Proof Loans, lending proof of reserves, and a $2.1 billion credit facility. Jack walks through his four-quadrant framework that separates real Bitcoin companies from crypto casinos and treasury-only plays. If you care about Bitcoin-backed credit, mining, or capital markets strategy, this one is essential.

programme.title: Afroman | Bitcoin 2026

In this keynote, Michael Saylor reveals how Strategy engineered STRC, a Bitcoin-backed preferred stock that grew into the largest and most liquid preferred in the world in under eight months. Saylor breaks down the math behind 11.5% tax-deferred yields, why private credit is melting down, and how digital credit is set to cannibalize trillions in legacy capital markets.

programme.title: Keynote: Jack Mallers - The Bitcoin Company | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: What does the ideal Bitcoin company actually look like? In this Bitcoin 2026 keynote, Jack Mallers CEO of Strike and Twenty One wears both hats to unveil a strategic merger with Tether's mining arm Electron and a slate of new Strike products including Volatility Proof Loans, lending proof of reserves, and a $2.1 billion credit facility. Jack walks through his four-quadrant framework that separates real Bitcoin companies from crypto casinos and treasury-only plays. If you care about Bitcoin-backed credit, mining, or capital markets strategy, this one is essential.

programme.title: Afroman | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Afroman lit up the Bitcoin Conference stage in Las Vegas with a performance unlike anything else this year. After his house was raided and his money seized, he discovered that freedom of speech and Bitcoin were the tools he needed to fight back. In this set, he announces his 2028 presidential campaign, calls for jury trials in family court, and performs live renditions of "Because I Got High" and "Lemon Pound Cake." Don't miss this raw, hilarious, and unexpectedly powerful moment from Vegas.

programme.title: Tim Draper's Bitcoin Warning: A Run on the Banks Is Coming | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The dollar is changing faster than most people realize. In this powerful keynote from The Bitcoin Conference in Las Vegas, legendary venture capitalist Tim Draper of Draper Associates explains why holding Bitcoin has shifted from opportunity to necessity. Drawing from his Mount Gox losses, his record-setting U.S. Marshal's Office auction bid, and decades of experience in Silicon Valley, Draper lays out the case for a dollar-to-stablecoin-to-Bitcoin transition.

programme.title: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins Bitcoin 2026 Fireside Chat
programme.desc: For the first time in history, a sitting SEC Chairman took the stage at the Bitcoin Conference. Paul Atkins joins Perianne Boring of The Digital Chamber on the Nakamoto stage in Las Vegas to detail a complete 180 in how the agency views digital assets. He breaks down the new joint token taxonomy with the CFTC, the SEC's reinterpretation of the Howey Test, and the upcoming innovation exemption that will let firms experiment with on-chain securities and token fundraising in the United States. If you want to understand where U.S. digital asset regulation is actually heading, this is the conversation.

programme.title: Fireside: CFTC Chairman Mike Selig | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For more than a decade, Bitcoiners and developers have lived under regulatory uncertainty and sometimes outright hostility from Washington. In this fireside conversation, CFTC Chairman Mike Selig joins Gregory Xethalis to explain how the agency has used its first 100+ days to end regulation by enforcement, launch Project Crypto with the SEC, and protect software developers building on Bitcoin. Selig breaks down the new joint taxonomy guidance, the no-action letter for self-custodial wallets, and why pending market structure legislation is essential to future-proof the asset class.

programme.title: Code is Free Speech: Ending the War on Bitcoin | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For years, Bitcoin developers wrote code with one eye over their shoulder. That era is officially over. At Bitcoin 2026, Coinbase Chief Legal Officer Paul Grewal sits down with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel to break down the April 7, 2025 DOJ memo that ended regulation by prosecution and what it means for builders, platforms, and the future of digital asset policy in the United States. They get into Tornado Cash, Samourai Wallet, the FBI's offshore scam compound takedowns, and why both DOJ leaders are personally Bitcoin holders.

programme.title: Arthur Hayes Bitcoin 2026 Keynote: 21 Weeks Later
programme.desc: The Iran war, AI replacing knowledge workers, and a new Fed Chair pick have markets confused. Arthur Hayes thinks most macro analysts are reading the tea leaves wrong. In this presentation, the BitMEX co-founder walks through why he's turned bullish on Bitcoin, why Kevin Warsh isn't the hawk people fear, and how a quiet April 1st banking regulation could unleash trillions in fresh credit. Hayes lays out a year-end Bitcoin target of $125,000 and explains the wartime money-printing thesis driving him there

programme.title: From American Hashrate to Wall Street: How Bitcoin Benefits The U.S. | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Bitcoin just crossed the bridge into Wall Street and the boomer money is finally moving. In this Bitcoin Conference panel, Bloomberg's Eric Balchunas sits down with Eric Trump of American Bitcoin and John Koudounis of Calamos Investments to unpack the $60B Bitcoin ETF wave, the $146 trillion in advised assets still sidelined, and the $124 trillion generational wealth transfer about to reshape every portfolio. Eric Trump tells his debanking story and explains why the Trump Organization went all-in on Bitcoin. John Koudounis breaks down Calamos' 100%, 90%, and 80% protected Bitcoin ETFs.

programme.title: Mark Moss: Building a Personal Treasury with a Perpetual Bitcoin Machine | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: You bought the right asset, but are you playing the wrong game? At Bitcoin Vegas 2026, Mark Moss of Market Disruptors argues that most Bitcoiners are still operating with a fiat mindset and will quietly lose the wealth game even with Bitcoin in cold storage. He unpacks the Cantillon effect, the macro debt loop, and a five-step "Perpetual Bitcoin Machine" designed to build a personal treasury that compounds for generations. If you've ever wondered how much Bitcoin you need to retire, this talk reframes the entire question.

programme.title: How Will Bitcoin Behave with Global Uncertainty? | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The Fed is changing hands, the Middle East is on fire, and private credit is starting to crack. Natalie Brunell sits down with Danielle DiMartino Booth (QI Research), Joseph Wang (Fedguy.com), and Matt Hougan (Bitwise) for a no-holds-barred debate on how Bitcoin behaves when the global order gets shaky. They cover Kevin Warsh's incoming Fed chairmanship, stagflation risk, and why Wall Street might be far more complacent than it should be. If you care about where macro and Bitcoin intersect, this is essential viewing.

programme.title: What's the Price of Freedom? Ask "The Six Billion Dollar Man" | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: What happens when an award-winning documentary about Julian Assange wins Cannes and a Golden Globe and still no streamer or network will touch it? Filmmaker Eugene Jarecki joins Jack Dorsey at Bitcoin 2026 to reveal how the Bitcoin community is stepping in where legacy media refuses to. They trace the line from Wikileaks' 2011 banking blockade, through Edward Snowden, to a Global Watch Party designed to bypass media censorship entirely.

programme.title: The Wives & Mothers Carrying The Fight Against Injustice | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The state came for the men they loved and these three women stepped onto the battlefield. Lauren Rodriguez (wife of jailed Samourai Wallet co-founder Keonne Rodriguez), Janice McAfee (widow of John McAfee), and Lyn Ulbricht (mother of pardoned Silk Road founder Ross Ulbricht) sit down with Efrat Fenigson to talk pardons, privacy, and what it really takes to fight the U.S. government from the outside. This is one of the most powerful conversations on Bitcoin, civil liberties, and the war on privacy you'll hear all year. Watch, share, and don't forget the prisoners.

programme.title: Multiple Paths, One Asset: Spend, Borrow, or Hodl? | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Jack Mallers and Miles Suter rarely share a stage and when they do, the gloves come off. Danny Knowles moderates this panel on whether Bitcoin should be spent, borrowed against, or held forever, with Strike pushing dollar-denominated Lightning payments and Block rolling out Tap to Pay across every Square merchant in America. The conversation gets into Saylor's borrowing strategy, the chicken-and-egg problem of Bitcoin merchant adoption, and why card network rewards are the real obstacle. If you care about Bitcoin payments, lending, or the future of peer-to-peer cash, this one is essential.

programme.title: Paolo Ardoino Keynote: Tether - A Psychohistory Implementation | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: What if a stablecoin company was actually building the foundation for civilization? In this Bitcoin Conference talk, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino borrows from Isaac Asimov's Foundation to explain why Tether is investing in Bitcoin, peer-to-peer protocols, self-custodial wallets, and decentralized AI. He breaks down the open-source Resilience Stack: Hole Punch, Keet, WDK, and QVAC SDK and why 4 billion unbanked people are at the heart of the mission.

programme.title: Are We Getting More Clarity? | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The CLARITY Act could be the most consequential piece of Bitcoin and digital asset legislation in U.S. history, and it's hanging in the balance right now. In this panel from the Bitcoin Conference, Senators Cynthia Lummis and Bernie Moreno join Patrick Witt of the White House, Sam Kazemian of Frax, and Miles Jennings of A16z crypto to break down why market structure matters, what's at stake for Bitcoin, and how the Genius Act paved the way. They also discuss the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, the CFTC's role, and the geopolitical stakes of ceding crypto leadership to China.

programme.title: Senator Cynthia Lummis on the Clarity Act and America's Bitcoin Future | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Senator Cynthia Lummis takes the Bitcoin 2026 stage to deliver a clear message: the Clarity Act is heading to markup in May, and the United States is positioning itself as the global capital for Bitcoin. She walks through the early Senate battles including the absurd IRS attempt to classify software developers and miners as brokers and explains how the Bitcoin industry's response shaped policy. With her time in office winding down, this keynote is both a victory lap and a roadmap.
